title: Completeness tested by the walking-isomorphism restriction
statement:
Use homotopy Segal spaces and their homotopy categories $hX$ from [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence], and bisimplicial sets, vertical Reedy fibrancy and division notation from [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus]. Let $\mathcal J$ be the ordinary groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and let $J=N\mathcal J$ be its ordinary nerve. Let $u_0:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ select $0$. For every vertically Reedy fibrant homotopy Segal space $X$, completeness, meaning that $s_0:X_0\to X_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, is equivalent to the assertion that endpoint restriction
$$u_0\backslash X:J\backslash X\longrightarrow\Delta^0\backslash X=X_0$$
is a trivial Kan fibration. Here $X_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq X_1$ is the union of components representing isomorphisms in $hX$, and trivial Kan fibration has the meaning of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Lemma 4.2; comparison of the completeness convention with s_0:X_0 to X_eq from Rezk, https://arxiv.org/html/math/9811037, Theorem 6.2 and Proposition 6.4. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy result. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: First check the Segal convention required by the classifier. Restriction along any monomorphism is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus]. In particular $X_n=\Delta^n\backslash X$ is Kan (use $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$), each $d_i:X_1\to X_0$ is a Kan fibration (use a vertex inclusion), and $(d_1,d_0):X_1\to X_0^2$ is a Kan fibration (use $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$). Put $S_1=X_1$ and $S_n=S_{n-1}\times_{X_0}X_1$, matching the last target to the next source. These are Kan: the projection $S_n\to S_{n-1}$ is the pullback of the source fibration of $X_1$, and Kan fibrations are stable under pullback and composition, since their horn lifting problems pull back and compose. The last-target map $S_n\to X_0$ is also a fibration: projecting instead onto the last $X_1$ is the pullback of the last-target map for $S_{n-1}$, so induction and composition with $d_0$ apply. Let $T_1=X_1$ and let $T_n$ be the iterated path-model homotopy product specified by the homotopy Segal hypothesis on $X$. The path products $T_n$ are Kan by induction from the Kan assertion of [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. Give $T_n$ its last-target map by projection to its final $X_1$ followed by $d_0$. The constant-path map $S_n\to T_n$ preserves that final $X_1$ coordinate, so commutes strictly with the last-target maps to $X_0$. Inductively this map is a weak homotopy equivalence: $S_n\to P(S_{n-1}\to X_0,X_1\to X_0)$ is one by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], and the map from this path product to $T_n=P(T_{n-1}\to X_0,X_1\to X_0)$ is one by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], using the induction hypothesis and identities on $X_0,X_1$. The case $n=1$ is the identity. The assumed map $X_n\to T_n$ factors through $X_n\to S_n$. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], applied in the Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], therefore makes $X_n\to S_n$ a weak homotopy equivalence for every $n\geq2$. Vertical Reedy fibrancy is Reedy fibrancy of $n\mapsto X_n$ in the sense of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] for $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the Kan model structure: since $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union, hence the colimit, of the faces $\Delta^k\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ given by the proper injective maps $[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$, in each inner degree $q$ one has $(\partial\Delta^n\backslash X)_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(\partial\Delta^n\boxtimes\Delta^q,X)=\lim X_{k,q}=(M_nX)_q$, so $\delta_n\backslash X$ is the matching map $X_n\to M_nX$, which is therefore a Kan fibration. Thus $X$ is a Reedy-fibrant Segal space in the classifier's strict-product convention.

source.place: Section 4 (Reedy-fibrant Segal spaces); convention comparison uses Kerodon 0329 and 032B and Joyal–Tierney Proposition 2.5

proof.text: The strict mapping fiber at $(x,y)$ and the homotopy mapping fiber used to define $hX$ have the same $\pi_0$: apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to the cospan $X_1\xrightarrow{(d_1,d_0)}X_0^2\leftarrow\{(x,y)\}$, whose first leg is a Kan fibration by step 1. The constant-path comparison takes $s_0x$ to the same identity arrow. For composable vertices $f:x\to y$ and $g:y\to z$ in the strict fibers, choose $\sigma\in(X_2)_0$ restricting to $(f,g)$. Such a lift exists: restriction along the two-edge spine $\Delta^1\amalg_{\Delta^0}\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$ is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus], and a weak homotopy equivalence by step 1, so is trivial and surjective on vertices by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the meaning of trivial in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. The strict composite is represented by $d_1\sigma$. The homotopy Segal map sends this same $\sigma$ to $(f,g)$ with the constant path at $y$, so the homotopy-fiber composite is represented by the same $d_1\sigma$. Thus the morphism-set bijections preserve composition as well as identities. They give the same objects and a category isomorphism, so an edge is invertible in one homotopy category exactly when it is invertible in the other. In particular the union $X_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq X_1$ and the map $s_0$ in the assertion are those in [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-classifier].

source.place: Sections 5 and 6; strict-fiber versus path-model comparison

proof.text: Let $t:J\to\Delta^0$ be the collapse, let $a:\Delta^1\to J$ be the edge $0\to1$, and set $A=J\backslash X$, $c=t\backslash X:X_0\to A$ and $p=u_0\backslash X:A\to X_0$. The division definition gives, in inner degree $q$, $A_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(J\boxtimes\Delta^q,X)$. This is exactly $((X^E)_0)_q$ in [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-classifier]: its $E$ is $J$ made discrete in the inner direction, $F(0)$ is terminal, and $c\Delta^q=*\boxtimes\Delta^q$. The classifier applies by steps 1–2 and supplies a weak homotopy equivalence $\epsilon:A\to X_{\mathrm{eq}}$ induced by $a$, with the exact identity $\epsilon c=s_0$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2, with the collapse and edge maps of Section 6

proof.text: Since $\epsilon$ is a weak homotopy equivalence and $\epsilon c=s_0$, two-out-of-three gives $s_0$ a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $c$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus completeness defined by $s_0:X_0\to X_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is equivalent to the collapse-restriction condition used in Joyal–Tierney Lemma 4.2.

We have $tu_0=\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}$, so contravariance of the division construction gives $pc=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}$ exactly. The identity is a weak homotopy equivalence; two-out-of-three therefore says that $c$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $p$ is one. Together with step 4, completeness is equivalent to $p$ being a weak homotopy equivalence.

Finally $u_0:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ is a monomorphism: in every degree it selects the simplex all of whose vertices are $0$. Vertical Reedy fibrancy and [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus] make $p=u_0\backslash X$ a Kan fibration, without assuming completeness. In the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], a trivial fibration means a fibration which is also a weak homotopy equivalence, as stipulated in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Consequently $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence exactly when it is a trivial Kan fibration. Step 5 now proves both implications of the assertion.
